cards.title: Introduction to Python
cards.content:
Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its clear syntax and readability.

print("Hello, Python Developer!")

cards.title: Basic Data Types
cards.content: Python has various built-in data types. Numbers are represented by int and float, text by str, and truth values by bool.

content.text: To assign the value 10 to a variable named score, you write ___ = 10.

cards.title: Control Flow with If-Else
cards.content:
Conditional statements allow your program to make decisions based on data.

if x > 0:
    print("Positive")
else:
    print("Non-positive")

steps: If `if` is False, evaluate the first `elif` condition
If all conditions are False, execute the `else` block

cards.title: Defining Functions
cards.content:
Functions are reusable blocks of code defined using the def keyword.

def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}"

cards.title: Lists and Tuples
cards.content: Lists are mutable sequences, denoted by square brackets []. Tuples are immutable sequences, denoted by parentheses ().

cards.title: Summary of Fundamentals
cards.content: You have covered variables, basic data types, control flow, functions, and collections. You are now ready to build more complex Python applications!
